Comparatives to Talk About Job Positions, with Short Adjectives
You use comparatives to indicate the differences between things, people, animals or, in this specific case, job positions.
For instance, a Java Developer is better managing Web browsers than a Data Modeler.
And a Project Manager is stronger in communication skills than the professionals named before.
A Data Modeler must work harder than a DBA since the first one monitors the primary design until its final production.

Comparatives with short adjectives

Adjectives with one or two syllables are considered short adjectives.

To make a comparison with short adjectives add the suffix “er” to the adjective followed by the conjunction than:

Adjective + er + than + complement

Example:
  • I consider that my job as Java Developer is quite harder than the Project Manager job.

images.text: Speaker: Welcome to our annual IT conference. In this opportunity, we will discuss some important facts related to different jobs in the IT field. I want you to take notes because we will carry out an activity later. Let’s start! According to a recent survey, the hottest jobs in IT are Java Developer, .Net Developer, and Data Modeler. As you must know these jobs have specific differences. For instance, a Java Developer is better at managing Web browsers than a Data Modeler. A .Net Developer has to code faster than a Java Developer.

Attendee: Excuse me; is it easy for a company to find these kinds of professionals?
 Speaker: I would say that it’s easier to find a Java developer than a Net Developer or a Data Modeler.
 Attendee: What’s the difference between a Data Modeler and a Database Administrator?
Speaker:  A Data Modeler must work harder than a DBA since the first one monitors the primary design until its final production.
 Attendee:  What will be the panorama for IT jobs in the future?
 Speaker:  There will be more occupations in IT; it also depends on the upcoming events. But you can be sure that with the current boom of technology, people will need more new professionals that handle new technological challenges.

Speaker:   Well, I will conclude by asking you to write a short text whose title will be: Duties and responsibilities related to job positions in IT. You must describe some of the principal jobs and make a parallel between them. Don’t forget to name important duties such as developing applications, updating programs, testing platforms, making defrags, storing confidential information, solving cryptic codes, implementing projects, handling customers’ expectations and having problem-solving skills.
